reasoning_traces.think:
Hamstring injuries represent catastrophic failures in the musculoskeletal system under sprinting loads. Conservative management fails because it does not address the underlying geometric mismatch caused by tendon retraction, leading to persistent high strain rates that exceed the tissue's energy threshold. Surgical excision removes the damaged segment, shifting the failure mode to a lower-energy regime where the remaining tendon can safely operate. The rehabilitation protocol accelerates recovery by systematically increasing mechanical stimulus to promote collagen realignment and neuromuscular adaptation, allowing the athlete to achieve pre-injury performance levels faster than natural healing alone.
